results.content:
## The Real Issue Isn’t the AI

The frustration people feel when working with AI often comes from the same place as my moment in that Mexican pharmacy: miscommunication. The good news is that once you understand it’s not about having the “right” prompts or AI being broken, you can approach writing prompts differently.

Plan intentionally. Test systematically. Evaluate honestly. These practices work with any tool, any model, any LLM. They may not guarantee the results you expect, but they transform the process from guessing to learning. [...] When AI outputs aren’t what we expect, it can be easy to declare a model or AI overall as broken. On the opposite side, it’s tempting to place blame on the prompt writer for lacking the communication skills to clearly define what they want.

The real issue lies somewhere in the middle. Like humans, AI isn’t perfect and it never will be. In order to bridge this gap, we have to learn how to work with LLMs.

## You Need a Plan

When we write code, we know that if we write a function that takes in 2 numbers and adds them together, the return will be the sum of those 2 numbers. We know this because we’ve planned it that way. But before any of us could do this work almost in our sleep, we had to learn how. We had to understand the fundamentals. [...] Over the past few months, we at Rotational have been building a platform called Endeavor that’s specifically designed to make these practices easier for teams. It’s a tool built from the ground up to support planning, testing, and evaluation of AI agents for custom use cases. The principles behind it are the insights I’ve shared here. Those principles are what matter most, regardless of what tool you use.

### About This Post

Working with AI can feel like learning a new language. Discover why miscommunication with LLMs isn't about broken tools or bad prompts and how to bridge the gap toward a better understanding.

results.content:
Troubleshooting LLM prompts? It’s like trying to herd digital cats: frustrating, quirky, but oh-so-rewarding when they finally behave. From vague answers and hilarious hallucinations to unexpectedly high token costs and stubborn refusals, every glitch has a root cause and a fix. Just grab your digital duct tape and a paperclip! Whether it’s adding laser-like specificity, fine-tuning the Temperature, or breaking down complex tasks into bite-sized chunks, you’re the AI’s personal MacGyver. [...] Let’s not forget the financial side! Poorly constructed prompts can inflate costs in paid API services or just waste your precious time with irrelevant outputs. Effective troubleshooting doesn’t just improve the quality of your responses; it optimizes your workflow, saving your time, budget and sanity. Like teenagers, how you ask is as important as what you ask. You know they are capable, but you have to figure out how to get them to focus on the important task.

## Troubleshooting Common Prompting Problems: Your Prompt First-Aid kit

Alright, Houston, we have a problem. Despite the futuristic allure of AI, certain glitches stubbornly persist. We’re here to confront these everyday headaches directly, with the calm expertise of an IT guru who’s fixed it all before. [...] ### Check Model Limits and Settings: Know Your Tools

Always review your LLM provider’s documentation. Familiarize yourself with context window limits, safety filters, and any adjustable parameters. Misalignment with these crucial settings can cause outright refusals, unexpected behavior, or frustrating delays. Don’t try to fit a square peg in a round hole!

### Start Simple, Scale Up: The “Crawl, Walk, Run” Approach

Begin with the most basic prompt possible. Only add complexity (e.g., Chain-of-Thought, more detailed instructions) if your simpler methods aren’t delivering the desired results. This minimizes initial errors, saves tokens, and reduces the chance of getting tangled in a complex web of instructions too early.

results.title: PromptBridge: Cross-Model Prompt Transfer for Large Language Models
results.content: The core challenge is that the prompt pMs,T∗p^{\}\_{M\_{s},T}, which was optimal for MsM\_{s}, is no longer optimal for MtM\_{t}. Therefore, effective prompt recalibration or transfer is required to restore alignment between the prompt and the target model’s behavioral distribution. [...] To address this challenge, we introduce PromptBridge, a training-free framework that preserves prompt effectiveness under model switches, enabling cross-model prompt transfer without costly per-task or per-model re-optimization. PromptBridge requires only a small set of alignment tasks for calibration. It first applies Model-Adaptive Reflective Prompt Evolution (MAP-RPE) to obtain task- and model-specific optimal prompts via iterative reflective refinement and quantitative evaluation. Using the resulting calibrated prompt pairs for the source and target models, PromptBridge learns a cross-model prompt mapping. At test time, i.e., for an unseen task, given a source-model prompt, this mapping directly produces an optimized prompt for the target model. [...] Agent utilizes sample I/O from the problem description to rectify bugs in the generated code. We set the similar problems number k=5k=5 and the plan generation number t=5t=5 for HumanEval. In this setup, the default prompt is treated as the initial transfer point. While it is not explicitly optimized for the source model, it represents a human-crafted, general-purpose prompt, which we consider as the source prompt in this context.
